goal:
`getters.go` repeats the same section-and-key lookup in `Get`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` and `GetDuration`. Move it into one unexported method,

```go
func (c *Config) lookup(section, key string) (string, error)
```

and make all four getters use it, so that none of them reads `c.sections` directly any more.

This is a pure refactor. The exported API, every returned value and every error message must stay exactly as they are now. The tests run with `go test ./...`.

criteria.statement: Get, GetInt, GetBool and GetDuration all call one unexported method lookup(section, key string) (string, error), and none of them reads c.sections directly
The exported API, every returned value and every error message of the four getters are exactly as before the refactor

criteria.baseline: it must pass on the input snapshot, as a regression guard; interlock saw it pass there (run run-ca164aa8a3ce4575)

previous_result.summary:
I added `lookup(section, key)` to `getters.go`, and `Get`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` and `GetDuration` now all call it. Only `lookup` reads `c.sections`. `go test ./...` passes (run through `interlock check run`), and `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

`GetBool` words its missing-key error differently from the others ("key %q not set"). To keep that message exactly, `lookup` returns a small unexported `missingKeyError` for a missing key. `GetBool` detects it and writes its own message. The other getters pass the error through unchanged.

I recorded claims for all three criteria. `regression` is `tested`. `structure` and `behaviour` are only `static`: for `behaviour` I read the diff and the existing tests pass, but I added no new test for the error wording. Those two still need the independent verifier.
